source.text: בְּ֭נִי אִם־עָרַ֣בְתָּ לְרֵעֶ֑ךָ תָּקַ֖עְתָּ לַזָּ֣ר כַּפֶּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: My son, if you have stood surety for your fellow, struck to a stranger your palms,

en.L: My son, if you have stood surety for your neighbor, \q [if] you have struck your palms for a stranger,
en.B: My son, if you have guaranteed a loan for your neighbor \q and shaken hands on it for a stranger,
en.R: My son, maybe you have promised to pay someone else's debt if they cannot pay it. \q Maybe you shook hands on that promise.

fr.L: Mon fils, si tu t’es porté garant pour ton prochain, \q [si] tu as frappé dans tes mains pour un étranger,
fr.B: Mon fils, si tu t’es porté garant d’un prêt pour ton prochain \q et si tu t’y es engagé d’une poignée de main pour un étranger,
fr.R: Mon fils, tu as peut-être promis de payer la dette de quelqu’un s’il ne peut pas la payer. \q Tu as peut-être serré la main pour conclure cette promesse.

decisions.choice: stood surety: made yourself responsible for another's debt
decisions.reason: To stand surety (arab) was to promise to pay if the borrower did not, sometimes with one's own property or person as security (Genesis 43:9; Proverbs 11:15; 22:26–27).

decisions.choice: struck your palms: shaken hands to seal the pledge
decisions.reason: Striking hands was how such an agreement was sealed in public (17:18; 22:26).

decisions.choice: your neighbor ... a stranger: the borrower and the lender
alternatives: two names for the same person
decisions.reason: The two lines may name the same person in two ways, or the neighbor may be the borrower and the stranger the lender to whom the pledge was given. Either way the son has bound himself to others.

source.text: נוֹקַ֥שְׁתָּ בְאִמְרֵי־פִ֑יךָ נִ֝לְכַּ֗דְתָּ בְּאִמְרֵי־פִֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: you have been snared by [the] words of your mouth; you have been caught by [the] words of your mouth.

en.L: you have been snared by [the] words of your mouth; \q you have been caught by [the] words of your mouth.
en.B: the words of your mouth have snared you; \q what you said has caught you.
en.R: If you did, your own words have trapped you like an animal in a net.

fr.L: tu as été pris au piège par les paroles de ta bouche ; \q tu as été capturé par les paroles de ta bouche.
fr.B: les paroles de ta bouche t’ont pris au piège ; \q ce que tu as dit t’a capturé.
fr.R: Si tu l’as fait, tes propres paroles t’ont pris au piège, comme un animal dans un filet.

decisions.choice: snared ... caught: trapped like a hunted animal
decisions.reason: The verbs are hunters' words, and the picture returns in verse 5 (the gazelle and the bird). The son is caught by nothing but his own promise.

source.text: עֲשֵׂ֨ה זֹ֥את אֵפ֪וֹא׀בְּנִ֡י וְֽהִנָּצֵ֗ל כִּ֘י בָ֤אתָ בְכַף־רֵעֶ֑ךָ לֵ֥ךְ הִ֝תְרַפֵּ֗ס וּרְהַ֥ב רֵעֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do this, then, my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into [the] palm of your neighbor: go, humble yourself, and press your neighbors.

en.L: Do this, then, my son, and deliver yourself, \q for you have come into [the] palm of your neighbor: \q go, humble yourself, and press your neighbor.
en.B: So, my son, do this and get yourself free, \q since you have fallen into your neighbor's power: \q go and humble yourself, and keep pressing your neighbor.
en.R: So, my son, do this to get free, because now your neighbor has power over you. \q Go and humbly beg your neighbor to release you. Do not give up.

fr.L: Fais donc ceci, mon fils, et délivre-toi, \q car tu es venu dans la paume de ton prochain : \q va, humilie-toi et presse ton prochain.
fr.B: Alors, mon fils, fais ceci pour te libérer, \q puisque tu es tombé au pouvoir de ton prochain : \q va t’humilier et insiste auprès de ton prochain.
fr.R: Alors, mon fils, fais ceci pour te libérer, parce que ton voisin a maintenant du pouvoir sur toi. \q Va supplier humblement ton voisin de te libérer. N’abandonne pas.

decisions.choice: into the palm of your neighbor: into his power
decisions.reason: To come into someone's hand or palm is to be in their power.

decisions.choice: humble yourself and press: beg without pride and without stopping
decisions.reason: The first verb (hitrappes) may mean to throw oneself down, or to stamp about; the second (rahab) to press or pester. The son is to set his pride aside and plead until he is released.

decisions.choice: your neighbor: the one to whom the pledge was given
decisions.reason: The form here is plural, "your neighbors". It may mean the neighbor of verse 1, in a plural of emphasis, or anyone involved in the pledge. The verse as a whole speaks of one neighbor.

source.text: אַל־תִּתֵּ֣ן שֵׁנָ֣ה לְעֵינֶ֑יךָ וּ֝תְנוּמָ֗ה לְעַפְעַפֶּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not give sleep to your eyes and slumber to your eyelids.

en.L: Do not give sleep to your eyes, \q or slumber to your eyelids.
en.B: Give your eyes no sleep \q and your eyelids no rest.
en.R: Do not go to sleep. \q Do not even rest your eyes until you are free.

fr.L: Ne donne pas de sommeil à tes yeux, \q ni d’assoupissement à tes paupières.
fr.B: N’accorde pas de sommeil à tes yeux \q ni de repos à tes paupières.
fr.R: Ne va pas dormir. \q Ne ferme même pas les yeux avant d’être libre.

decisions.choice: no sleep: act at once
decisions.reason: The matter is urgent (Psalm 132:4). The sluggard of verses 9–10 does the opposite.

source.text: הִ֭נָּצֵל כִּצְבִ֣י מִיָּ֑ד וּ֝כְצִפּ֗וֹר מִיַּ֥ד יָקֽוּשׁ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Deliver yourself like a gazelle from [the] hand, and like a bird from [the] hand of a fowler.

en.L: Deliver yourself like a gazelle from [the] hand, \q and like a bird from [the] hand of [the] fowler.
en.B: Get yourself free like a gazelle from the hunter's grip, \q like a bird from the hand of the one who traps it.
en.R: Escape like a deer running from a hunter, \q or like a bird flying away from a trap.

fr.L: Délivre-toi comme une gazelle de la main, \q et comme un oiseau de la main de l’oiseleur.
fr.B: Libère-toi comme une gazelle de la poigne du chasseur, \q comme un oiseau de la main de celui qui le piège.
fr.R: Échappe-toi comme une biche qui fuit devant un chasseur, \q ou comme un oiseau qui s’envole loin d’un piège.

decisions.choice: from the hand: the hunter's hand
decisions.reason: The first line says only "from the hand"; the second line shows whose hand it is. Some suggest a small change that gives "from the trap".

source.text: לֵֽךְ־אֶל־נְמָלָ֥ה עָצֵ֑ל רְאֵ֖ה דְרָכֶ֣יהָ וַחֲכָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Go to [the] ant, sluggard; see her ways and be wise,

en.L: Go to [the] ant, sluggard; \q see her ways and be wise,
en.B: You lazy one, go and look at the ant; \q watch how it lives, and learn wisdom.
en.R: You lazy person, go and watch the ants. \q Learn from what they do, and become wise.

fr.L: Va vers la fourmi, paresseux ; \q vois ses voies et sois sage,
fr.B: Toi, le paresseux, va regarder la fourmi ; \q observe comment elle vit, et deviens sage.
fr.R: Toi qui es paresseux, va regarder les fourmis. \q Apprends de ce qu’elles font, et deviens sage.

decisions.choice: sluggard: the lazy person
decisions.reason: The sluggard (atsel) is a figure Proverbs comes back to often (10:26; 19:24; 26:13–16): someone who always has a reason not to work.

decisions.choice: the ant: a small creature that works ahead
decisions.reason: The ant is one of the "small but wise" creatures of 30:24–25, which store their food in summer.

decisions.choice: lazy one (B); lazy person (R)
decisions.reason: "Sluggard" is little used in modern English. Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: "le paresseux" for the sluggard (ʿatsel), for the whole book
decisions.reason: "Paresseux" is the plain French word at every level; "fainéant" is more colloquial and "indolent" too literary.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֖ר אֵֽין־לָ֥הּ קָצִ֗ין שֹׁטֵ֥ר וּמֹשֵֽׁל׃

records.literal_gloss: which has no commander, officer or ruler,

en.L: which has no commander, officer, or ruler,
en.B: It has no chief, no overseer and no ruler,
en.R: Ants do not have a leader or a boss telling them what to do.

fr.L: elle qui n’a ni chef, ni surveillant, ni maître,
fr.B: Elle n’a ni chef, ni contremaître, ni maître,
fr.R: Les fourmis n’ont pas de chef ni de patron qui leur dit quoi faire.

decisions.choice: commander, officer, ruler: anyone to give orders
decisions.reason: Three words for those in charge: a leader (qatsin), an official who keeps records or gives orders (shoter, Exodus 5:6), and a ruler (moshel).

source.text: תָּכִ֣ין בַּקַּ֣יִץ לַחְמָ֑הּ אָגְרָ֥ה בַ֝קָּצִ֗יר מַאֲכָלָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: She prepares in summer her food; she gathers in harvest her provision.

en.L: [yet] she prepares her food in summer; \q she gathers her provision at harvest.
en.B: yet it gets its food ready in summer \q and gathers its supplies at harvest time.
en.R: But they get their food ready in the summer. \q They gather it during harvest time.

fr.L: [pourtant] elle prépare en été sa nourriture ; \q elle amasse pendant la moisson ses provisions.
fr.B: pourtant elle prépare sa nourriture en été \q et rassemble ses provisions au temps de la moisson.
fr.R: Mais elles préparent leur nourriture pendant l’été. \q Elles la ramassent au moment de la moisson.

decisions.choice: prepares ... gathers: work done ahead of need
decisions.reason: The ant works when the food is there, without being told, so that it has enough later.

decisions.choice: the verse ends here, as the Hebrew text has it
alternatives: a further passage on the bee (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation adds several lines after this verse about the bee as another example to learn from. They are not in the Hebrew text.

source.text: עַד־מָתַ֖י עָצֵ֥ל׀תִּשְׁכָּ֑ב מָ֝תַ֗י תָּק֥וּם מִשְּׁנָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Until when, sluggard, will you lie down? When will you rise from your sleep?

en.L: Until when, sluggard, will you lie down? \q When will you rise from your sleep?
en.B: Lazy one, how long will you stay lying there? \q When will you rise from sleeping?
en.R: You lazy person, how long will you lie in bed? \q When will you get up?

fr.L: Jusqu’à quand, paresseux, resteras-tu couché ? \q Quand te lèveras-tu de ton sommeil ?
fr.B: Paresseux, combien de temps resteras-tu couché là ? \q Quand sortiras-tu de ton sommeil ?
fr.R: Toi qui es paresseux, combien de temps vas-tu rester au lit ? \q Quand vas-tu te lever ?

decisions.choice: until when ... when: impatience
decisions.reason: The two questions, like Wisdom's in 1:22, show the father's impatience.

source.text: מְעַ֣ט שֵׁ֭נוֹת מְעַ֣ט תְּנוּמ֑וֹת מְעַ֓ט׀חִבֻּ֖ק יָדַ֣יִם לִשְׁכָּֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of hands to rest,

en.L: A little sleep, a little slumber, \q a little folding of [the] hands to rest,
en.B: "A bit more sleep, a bit more dozing, \q a bit more lying with arms folded,"
en.R: You say, "Let me sleep a little longer. \q Let me rest a little more."

fr.L: Un peu de sommeil, un peu d’assoupissement, \q un peu croiser les mains pour se reposer,
fr.B: « Encore un peu de sommeil, encore un peu de somnolence, \q encore un peu les bras croisés, allongé »,
fr.R: Tu dis : « Laisse-moi dormir encore un peu. \q Laisse-moi me reposer encore un peu. »

decisions.choice: a little sleep: the sluggard's own words
decisions.reason: The line sounds like the sluggard's answer to verse 9. Each time he asks for only a little more.

decisions.choice: repeated in 24:33–34
decisions.reason: Verses 10–11 come again almost word for word at the end of the story of the sluggard's field (24:30–34).

source.text: וּבָֽא־כִמְהַלֵּ֥ךְ רֵאשֶׁ֑ךָ וּ֝מַחְסֹֽרְךָ֗ כְּאִ֣ישׁ מָגֵֽן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and will come like a traveler your poverty, and your want like a man of shield.

en.L: and your poverty will come like a vagrant, \q and your need like a man with a shield.
en.B: and poverty will be on you like a drifter on the road, \q and need like a man with a shield.
en.R: Then you will suddenly become poor, \q as if a robber had come and taken everything you have.

fr.L: et ta pauvreté viendra comme un vagabond, \q et ton dénuement comme un homme armé d’un bouclier.
fr.B: et la pauvreté tombera sur toi comme un rôdeur sur la route, \q et le besoin comme un homme armé.
fr.R: Alors tu deviendras pauvre d’un coup, \q comme si un voleur était venu prendre tout ce que tu as.

decisions.choice: a vagrant ... a man with a shield: a raider
decisions.reason: The first word (mehallek) is one who walks about, a wanderer or highwayman; the second is an armed man. Poverty arrives unannounced and cannot be fought off.

decisions.choice: as if a robber had come
alternatives: like a vagrant ... like a man with a shield
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two pictures into one plain comparison.

source.text: אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A person of worthlessness, a man of wickedness, [is] walking [with] crookedness of mouth,

en.L: A person of worthlessness, {{gender:a person|a man}} of wickedness, \q [goes] walking with crookedness of mouth,
en.B: A scoundrel, a troublemaker, \q goes about with twisted speech,
en.R: A worthless, evil person goes around telling lies.

fr.L: Une personne de rien, {{gender:une personne|un homme}} de méchanceté, \q [s’en] va avec une bouche tortueuse,
fr.B: Un vaurien, un malfaisant, \q s’en va avec des paroles tordues,
fr.R: Une personne mauvaise et bonne à rien passe son temps à mentir.

decisions.choice: worthlessness: utter good-for-nothing
decisions.reason: The word (beliyyaal) means worthless or wicked, used of men who do great evil (Judges 19:22; 1 Samuel 2:12). Later it became a name for Satan (2 Corinthians 6:15), but here it describes a man.

decisions.choice: wickedness: trouble, harm
decisions.reason: The word (awen) is wrongdoing that causes harm to others (6:18; 12:21).

source.text: קֹרֵ֣ץ בְּ֭עֵינָומֹלֵ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֑ומֹ֝רֶ֗ה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: winking with his eyes, scraping with his foot, pointing with his fingers,

en.L: winking with {{gender:their|his}} eyes, scraping with {{gender:their|his}} foot, \q pointing with {{gender:their|his}} fingers,
en.B: winking with the eye, shuffling the feet, \q signaling with the fingers,
en.R: This person winks, makes signs with the feet, \q and points with the fingers to fool people.

fr.L: clignant de ses yeux, frottant de son pied, \q pointant de ses doigts,
fr.B: il cligne de l’œil, traîne les pieds, \q fait des signes avec les doigts,
fr.R: Cette personne fait des clins d’œil, des signes avec les pieds \q et montre du doigt pour tromper les gens.

decisions.choice: winking, scraping, pointing: secret signals
decisions.reason: These are signs passed to partners in a plot, behind someone's back (10:10; 16:30; Psalm 35:19).

source.text: תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת׀בְּלִבּ֗וֹ חֹרֵ֣שׁ רָ֣ע בְּכָל־עֵ֑ת מִדְיָנִ֥ים יְשַׁלֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: perversities [are] in his heart; [he is] devising evil at every time; contentions he sends out.

en.L: perversities [are] in {{gender:their|his}} heart, \q devising evil at all times; \q {{gender:they|he}} sends out quarrels.
en.B: with a heart full of deceit, always planning harm \q and stirring up quarrels.
en.R: Such a person is always planning to do something bad \q and always starting fights.

fr.L: des perversités [sont] dans son cœur, \q il trame le mal en tout temps ; \q il répand des querelles.
fr.B: le cœur plein de ruse, il prépare sans cesse le mal \q et provoque des disputes.
fr.R: Une telle personne cherche toujours à faire quelque chose de mal \q et elle provoque toujours des disputes.

decisions.choice: quarrels, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) and the reading the scribes marked (qere) give two forms of the word "quarrels"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: perversities: twisted things
decisions.reason: The word (tahpukot) of 2:12, 14: what turns things upside down.

source.text: עַל־כֵּ֗ן פִּ֭תְאֹם יָב֣וֹא אֵיד֑וֹ פֶּ֥תַע יִ֝שָּׁבֵ֗ר וְאֵ֣ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Therefore suddenly will come his disaster; [in] an instant he will be broken, and there [will] not [be] healing.

en.L: Therefore {{gender:their|his}} disaster will come suddenly; \q in an instant {{gender:they|he}} will be broken, \q and there [will be] no healing.
en.B: So disaster will come on such a person suddenly, \q and in a moment break them beyond healing.
en.R: So trouble will come suddenly on such people, and they will be destroyed in a moment. \q Nothing will help them.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi son désastre viendra soudain ; \q en un instant il sera brisé, \q et il n’y [aura] pas de guérison.
fr.B: Aussi le désastre fondra-t-il soudain sur lui, \q et en un instant il sera brisé sans remède.
fr.R: Alors le malheur tombera soudain sur ces gens, et ils seront détruits en un instant. \q Rien ne pourra les aider.

decisions.choice: broken, and no healing: ruined for good
decisions.reason: The same words end 29:1: a sudden fall from which there is no recovery.

source.text: שֶׁשׁ־הֵ֭נָּה שָׂנֵ֣א יְהוָ֑ה וְ֝שֶׁ֗בַע תּוֹעֲבַ֥תנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Six [things] these YHWH hates, and seven [are] an abomination of his soul:

en.L: Six [things] these {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hates, \q and seven [are] an abomination to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} soul:
en.B: Six things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hates, \q and seven {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} detests with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} whole being:
en.R: Here are six things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hates. \q Here are seven things that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot stand:

fr.L: Six [choses], celles-ci, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} les hait, \q et sept [sont] une abomination pour {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} âme :
fr.B: Il y a six choses que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} hait, \q et sept qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} déteste de tout {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} être :
fr.R: Voici six choses que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} déteste. \q Voici sept choses qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne peut pas supporter :

decisions.choice: six ... seven: a numbered saying
decisions.reason: "Six ... seven" is a way of building a list to its climax, with the last item weighed most (30:15–31; Amos 1:3). Here the seventh, sowing discord, ties back to verse 14.

decisions.choice: an abomination, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) are plural; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is singular. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: an abomination to his soul: what he detests
decisions.reason: Abomination (toevah) as in 3:32. "His soul" (nephesh) means his whole self.

source.text: עֵינַ֣יִם רָ֭מוֹת לְשׁ֣וֹן שָׁ֑קֶר וְ֝יָדַ֗יִם שֹׁפְכ֥וֹת דָּם־נָקִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: eyes haughty, a tongue of falsehood, and hands shedding blood innocent,

en.L: haughty eyes, a tongue of falsehood, \q and hands that shed innocent blood,
en.B: eyes that look down on others, a tongue that tells lies, \q hands that spill innocent blood,
en.R: people who think they are better than others, people who tell lies, \q people who kill innocent people,

fr.L: des yeux hautains, une langue de mensonge, \q et des mains qui versent le sang innocent,
fr.B: des yeux qui regardent les autres de haut, une langue qui ment, \q des mains qui répandent le sang innocent,
fr.R: les gens qui se croient meilleurs que les autres, les gens qui mentent, \q les gens qui tuent des innocents,

decisions.choice: haughty eyes: pride
decisions.reason: Literally "lifted eyes": the look of someone who looks down on others (30:13; Psalm 18:28).

decisions.choice: people who ...
decisions.reason: Readable names the people rather than the parts of the body, which young readers may take literally.

source.text: לֵ֗ב חֹ֭רֵשׁ מַחְשְׁב֣וֹת אָ֑וֶן רַגְלַ֥יִם מְ֝מַהֲר֗וֹת לָר֥וּץ לָֽרָעָה׃

records.literal_gloss: a heart devising plans of wickedness, feet hurrying to run to evil,

en.L: a heart devising plans of wickedness, \q feet hurrying to run to evil,
en.B: a heart that works out wicked plans, \q feet in a hurry to run to evil,
en.R: people who plan to do evil, \q people who rush to do wrong,

fr.L: un cœur qui trame des projets de méchanceté, \q des pieds qui se hâtent de courir au mal,
fr.B: un cœur qui prépare des plans malfaisants, \q des pieds pressés de courir vers le mal,
fr.R: les gens qui préparent de mauvais plans, \q les gens qui se dépêchent de faire le mal,

decisions.choice: feet hurrying to evil: as in 1:16
decisions.reason: The gang of 1:16 had feet that "run to evil".

source.text: יָפִ֣יחַ כְּ֭זָבִים עֵ֣ד שָׁ֑קֶר וּמְשַׁלֵּ֥חַ מְ֝דָנִ֗ים בֵּ֣ין אַחִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [one who] breathes out lies, a witness of falsehood, and [one] sending out contentions between brothers.

en.L: a witness of falsehood [who] breathes out lies, \q and one who sends out quarrels between {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.B: a false witness who breathes out lies, \q and one who sows quarrels among {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}.
en.R: people who lie in court, \q and people who make family members fight with each other.

fr.L: un témoin de mensonge [qui] souffle des faussetés, \q et celui qui répand des querelles entre {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.B: un faux témoin qui souffle des mensonges, \q et celui qui sème la discorde entre {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}.
fr.R: les gens qui mentent au tribunal, \q et les gens qui font se disputer les membres d’une même famille.

decisions.choice: a false witness: one who lies in court
decisions.reason: Giving false witness breaks the ninth commandment (Exodus 20:16) and could cost an innocent life (Deuteronomy 19:16–19).

decisions.choice: brothers: members of a family or community
decisions.reason: The word (ahim) is used of kin and of fellow members of the people (Psalm 133:1). The last item returns to the troublemaker of verse 14.

source.text: נְצֹ֣ר בְּ֭נִי מִצְוַ֣ת אָבִ֑יךָ וְאַל־תִּ֝טֹּ֗שׁ תּוֹרַ֥ת אִמֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Keep, my son, [the] commandment of your father, and do not forsake [the] teaching of your mother.

en.L: Keep, my son, [the] command of your father, \q and do not let go [of the] teaching of your mother.
en.B: My son, hold on to your father's command \q and do not let go of what your mother teaches you.
en.R: My son, obey your father's commands. \q Do not turn away from what your mother teaches you.

fr.L: Garde, mon fils, le commandement de ton père, \q et ne délaisse pas l’enseignement de ta mère.
fr.B: Mon fils, tiens ferme au commandement de ton père \q et ne laisse pas de côté ce que ta mère t’enseigne.
fr.R: Mon fils, obéis aux commandements de ton père. \q Ne te détourne pas de ce que ta mère t’apprend.

decisions.choice: your father's command and your mother's teaching: as in 1:8
decisions.reason: The words echo 1:8, at the head of a new warning about adultery (verses 24–35).

source.text: קָשְׁרֵ֣ם עַל־לִבְּךָ֣ תָמִ֑יד עָ֝נְדֵ֗ם עַל־גַּרְגְּרֹתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Bind them on your heart continually; tie them on your neck.

en.L: Bind them on your heart continually; \q tie them on your neck.
en.B: Keep them tied to your heart at all times; \q wear them knotted around your neck.
en.R: Always keep them in your heart. \q Hold on to them as if they were tied around your neck.

fr.L: Lie-les sur ton cœur continuellement ; \q attache-les à ton cou.
fr.B: Garde-les attachés à ton cœur en tout temps ; \q porte-les noués autour du cou.
fr.R: Garde-les toujours dans ton cœur. \q Tiens-les bien, comme s’ils étaient attachés à ton cou.

decisions.choice: bind ... tie: as in 3:3 and Deuteronomy 6:8
decisions.reason: The picture of 3:3: the teaching worn close, never out of reach.

source.text: בְּהִתְהַלֶּכְךָ֨׀תַּנְחֶ֬ה אֹתָ֗ךְ בְּֽ֭שָׁכְבְּךָ תִּשְׁמֹ֣ר עָלֶ֑יךָ וַ֝הֲקִיצ֗וֹתָ הִ֣יא תְשִׂיחֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: When you walk about, it will guide you; when you lie down, it will watch over you; and you awake, it will talk with you.

en.L: When you walk about, it will guide you; \q when you lie down, it will watch over you; \q and [when] you wake, it will talk with you.
en.B: As you walk, it will lead you; \q as you lie down, it will keep watch over you; \q and when you wake, it will talk with you.
en.R: When you walk, it will show you the way. \q When you sleep, it will protect you. \q When you wake up, it will teach you.

fr.L: Quand tu marcheras, il te guidera ; \q quand tu te coucheras, il veillera sur toi ; \q et [quand] tu te réveilleras, il parlera avec toi.
fr.B: Quand tu marcheras, cet enseignement te conduira ; \q quand tu te coucheras, il veillera sur toi ; \q et quand tu te réveilleras, il parlera avec toi.
fr.R: Quand tu marcheras, il te montrera le chemin. \q Quand tu dormiras, il te protégera. \q Quand tu te réveilleras, il t’instruira.

decisions.choice: it: the teaching as a whole
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular though verse 21 says "them". The command and teaching are taken together as one guide, perhaps with Wisdom in mind.

decisions.choice: walking, lying down, waking: as in Deuteronomy 6:7
decisions.reason: Israel was to talk about God's words "when you walk by the way, when you lie down and when you rise".

decisions.choice: "il" refers to the teaching as a whole; Balanced names it ("cet enseignement")
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "it" is the teaching of father and mother together (meaning decision m1). French "il" reads naturally as "l'enseignement", and Balanced says so to avoid a bare pronoun after a plural "them" in verse 21.

source.text: כִּ֤י נֵ֣ר מִ֭צְוָה וְת֣וֹרָה א֑וֹר וְדֶ֥רֶךְ חַ֝יִּ֗ים תּוֹכְח֥וֹת מוּסָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: For a lamp [is the] commandment, and [the] teaching [is] a light, and a way of life [are] rebukes of discipline,

en.L: For a command [is] a lamp, and teaching [is] a light, \q and [the] rebukes of discipline [are the] way of life,
en.B: For a command is a lamp and teaching is a light, \q and the warnings that discipline brings are the road to life,
en.R: Commands and teaching are like a lamp that lights your way. \q Correction shows you how to live.

fr.L: Car le commandement [est] une lampe, et l’enseignement [est] une lumière, \q et les réprimandes de la discipline [sont] le chemin de la vie,
fr.B: Car le commandement est une lampe et l’enseignement une lumière, \q et les avertissements qu’apporte la discipline sont le chemin de la vie,
fr.R: Les commandements et l’enseignement sont comme une lampe qui éclaire ton chemin. \q La correction te montre comment vivre.

decisions.choice: lamp ... light: as in Psalm 119:105
decisions.reason: "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path." The father's teaching works as God's word does.

source.text: לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת רָ֑ע מֵֽ֝חֶלְקַ֗ת לָשׁ֥וֹן נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: to keep you from a woman of evil, from [the] smoothness of tongue of a foreign [woman].

en.L: to keep you from [the] woman of evil, \q from [the] smoothness of tongue of a foreign [woman].
en.B: to guard you from the evil woman \q and the smooth tongue of the outsider.
en.R: They will keep you away from a wicked woman and her sweet talk.

fr.L: pour te garder de la femme mauvaise, \q de la douceur de langue de l’étrangère.
fr.B: pour te protéger de la femme mauvaise \q et de la langue doucereuse de l’étrangère.
fr.R: Ils te garderont loin d’une femme méchante et de ses belles paroles.

decisions.choice: the evil woman, as the Hebrew vowels read
alternatives: your neighbor's wife (other vowels, and the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The same consonants, with other vowels, read "the wife of a neighbor". The ancient Greek translation reads "a married woman". The verses that follow (29) are about a neighbor's wife, so the sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: foreign: an outsider
decisions.reason: The word (nokriyyah) of 2:16 and 5:20.

source.text: אַל־תַּחְמֹ֣ד יָ֭פְיָהּ בִּלְבָבֶ֑ךָ וְאַל־תִּ֝קָּֽחֲךָ֗ בְּעַפְעַפֶּֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not desire her beauty in your heart, and do not let her capture you with her eyelids,

en.L: Do not desire her beauty in your heart, \q and do not let her capture you with her eyelids,
en.B: Do not let your heart crave her beauty, \q and do not let her catch you with her glances,
en.R: Do not let yourself want her because she is beautiful. \q Do not let her catch you with the way she looks at you.

fr.L: Ne désire pas sa beauté dans ton cœur, \q et qu’elle ne te prenne pas par ses paupières,
fr.B: Que ton cœur ne convoite pas sa beauté, \q et ne te laisse pas prendre par ses regards,
fr.R: Ne te mets pas à la désirer parce qu’elle est belle. \q Ne te laisse pas prendre par la façon dont elle te regarde.

decisions.choice: desire: the word of the tenth commandment
decisions.reason: The verb (hamad) is the one in "you shall not covet your neighbor's wife" (Exodus 20:17).

decisions.choice: her eyelids: her glances
decisions.reason: Her eyes are her net (compare 6:13 and 4:25); she catches with a look.

source.text: כִּ֤י בְעַד־אִשָּׁ֥ה זוֹנָ֗ה עַֽד־כִּכַּ֫ר לָ֥חֶם וְאֵ֥שֶׁת אִ֑ישׁ נֶ֖פֶשׁ יְקָרָ֣ה תָצֽוּד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: for [the] price of a woman, a prostitute, [is] to a loaf of bread, but [the] wife of a man hunts a precious life.

en.L: for [the] price of a prostitute [is] up to a loaf of bread, \q but a man's wife hunts a precious life.
en.B: For a prostitute's price may be only a loaf of bread, \q but a married woman stalks a man's whole life.
en.R: Going to a prostitute may cost you only a loaf of bread. \q But going to another man's wife can cost you your life.

fr.L: car le prix d’une prostituée [va] jusqu’à une miche de pain, \q mais la femme d’un homme chasse une vie précieuse.
fr.B: Car une prostituée ne coûte parfois qu’une miche de pain, \q mais une femme mariée traque la vie même d’un homme.
fr.R: Aller chez une prostituée peut te coûter seulement un pain. \q Mais aller avec la femme d’un autre peut te coûter la vie.

decisions.choice: the price of a prostitute is a loaf of bread
alternatives: because of a prostitute a man is brought down to a loaf of bread
decisions.reason: The line is short and hard. It may mean that a prostitute costs little, or that she leaves a man with nothing but a loaf of bread. The point is the contrast with the second line: another man's wife costs a man his life. Neither line approves of the first.

decisions.choice: a man's wife: another man's wife
decisions.reason: The phrase means a married woman, as verse 29 makes plain.

source.text: הֲיַחְתֶּ֤ה אִ֓ישׁ אֵ֬שׁ בְּחֵיק֑וֹ וּ֝בְגָדָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִשָּׂרַֽפְנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Can a man snatch up fire in his bosom, and his garments not be burned?

en.L: Can a man scoop up fire into his bosom, \q and his garments not be burned?
en.B: Can a man carry fire against his chest \q and not set his clothes alight?
en.R: If a man holds fire against his body, \q his clothes will burn.

fr.L: Un homme peut-il prendre du feu dans son sein \q sans que ses vêtements brûlent ?
fr.B: Un homme peut-il porter du feu contre sa poitrine \q sans que ses habits prennent feu ?
fr.R: Si un homme tient du feu contre son corps, \q ses vêtements brûleront.

decisions.choice: fire ... bosom: wordplay
decisions.reason: Fire (esh) sounds like the word for man (ish) and woman (ishah). The bosom is the fold of a garment at the chest, and also where one holds a wife (5:20).

source.text: אִם־יְהַלֵּ֣ךְ אִ֭ישׁ עַל־הַגֶּחָלִ֑ים וְ֝רַגְלָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִכָּוֶֽינָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Or can a man walk on the coals, and his feet not be scorched?

en.L: Or can a man walk on the coals, \q and his feet not be scorched?
en.B: Or can a man walk over live coals \q and his feet not be burned?
en.R: If he walks on hot coals, \q his feet will be burned.

fr.L: Ou un homme peut-il marcher sur les braises \q sans que ses pieds soient brûlés ?
fr.B: Ou un homme peut-il marcher sur des charbons ardents \q sans se brûler les pieds ?
fr.R: S’il marche sur des braises, \q il se brûlera les pieds.

decisions.choice: or can a man: the answer is no
decisions.reason: The two questions expect "no" and lead to verse 29.

source.text: כֵּ֗ן הַ֭בָּא אֶל־אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֑הוּ לֹ֥א יִ֝נָּקֶ֗ה כָּֽל־הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: So [is] the one going in to [the] wife of his neighbor; not will go unpunished anyone touching her.

en.L: So [is] the one who goes in to his neighbor's wife; \q everyone who touches her will not go unpunished.
en.B: It is the same with the man who sleeps with his neighbor's wife: \q anyone who touches her will pay for it.
en.R: In the same way, a man who sleeps with his neighbor's wife will be punished.

fr.L: Ainsi [en est-il de] celui qui va vers la femme de son prochain ; \q quiconque la touche ne restera pas impuni.
fr.B: Il en va de même pour l’homme qui couche avec la femme de son prochain : \q quiconque la touche le paiera.
fr.R: De la même façon, un homme qui couche avec la femme de son voisin sera puni.

decisions.choice: goes in to: has sexual relations with
decisions.reason: As in 2:19.

decisions.choice: will not go unpunished: will not be held innocent
decisions.reason: The verb (naqah) means to be declared free of guilt (11:21; Exodus 20:7).

source.text: לֹא־יָב֣וּזוּ לַ֭גַּנָּב כִּ֣י יִגְנ֑וֹב לְמַלֵּ֥א נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ כִּ֣י יִרְעָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: They do not despise a thief when he steals to fill his appetite when he is hungry,

en.L: They do not despise a thief when he steals \q to fill his appetite when he is hungry,
en.B: People do not despise a thief who steals \q to fill an empty stomach when he is starving,
en.R: People may not hate a man who steals food because he is starving.

fr.L: On ne méprise pas un voleur quand il vole \q pour remplir son appétit quand il a faim,
fr.B: On ne méprise pas le voleur qui vole \q pour remplir son estomac quand il meurt de faim,
fr.R: Les gens ne détestent peut-être pas un homme qui vole de la nourriture parce qu’il meurt de faim.

decisions.choice: they do not despise: or "do they not despise?"
alternatives: Do they not despise a thief ...?
decisions.reason: The line may be a statement (people understand a hungry thief) or a question (people despise even a hungry thief). Either way verse 31 says he must still pay, and the adulterer is far worse off.

decisions.choice: appetite: his hunger
decisions.reason: The word (nephesh) here is the throat or appetite (Isaiah 5:14).

source.text: וְ֭נִמְצָא יְשַׁלֵּ֣ם שִׁבְעָתָ֑יִם אֶת־כָּל־ה֖וֹן בֵּית֣וֹ יִתֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: and [if] he is found, he will repay sevenfold; all [the] wealth of his house he will give.

en.L: yet [if] he is caught, he will repay sevenfold; \q all [the] wealth of his house he will give.
en.B: yet if he is caught he must pay back seven times over, \q even if it takes everything in his house.
en.R: But if he is caught, he must pay back seven times what he stole, \q even if he has to give everything he owns.

fr.L: et [s’]il est pris, il rendra sept fois ; \q tous les biens de sa maison il donnera.
fr.B: mais s’il est pris, il doit rendre sept fois plus, \q même s’il lui faut donner tout ce qu’il a chez lui.
fr.R: Mais s’il se fait prendre, il doit rendre sept fois ce qu’il a volé, \q même s’il doit donner tout ce qu’il possède.

decisions.choice: sevenfold: full repayment
decisions.reason: The law set repayment at two, four or five times the value (Exodus 22:1–4). Seven is the number of completeness: he pays in full, whatever it costs.

source.text: נֹאֵ֣ף אִשָּׁ֣ה חֲסַר־לֵ֑ב מַֽשְׁחִ֥ית נַ֝פְשׁ֗וֹ ה֣וּא יַעֲשֶֽׂנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: [One] committing adultery [with] a woman [is] lacking of heart; [one] destroying his life, he does it.

en.L: One who commits adultery [with] a woman [is] lacking heart; \q one who destroys his own life [is the one who] does it.
en.B: But a man who commits adultery has no sense; \q only someone bent on destroying himself would do it.
en.R: But a man who sleeps with another man's wife is a fool. \q He is destroying himself.

fr.L: Celui qui commet l’adultère [avec] une femme manque de cœur ; \q celui qui détruit sa propre vie, [c’est lui qui] fait cela.
fr.B: Mais l’homme qui commet l’adultère n’a pas de bon sens ; \q seul celui qui veut se détruire agit ainsi.
fr.R: Mais un homme qui couche avec la femme d’un autre est un insensé. \q Il se détruit lui-même.

decisions.choice: lacking heart: without sense
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of understanding (2:2); to lack heart is to lack judgment (7:7; 9:4).

source.text: נֶֽגַע־וְקָל֥וֹן יִמְצָ֑א וְ֝חֶרְפָּת֗וֹ לֹ֣א תִמָּחֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: A wound and dishonor he will find, and his reproach will not be wiped away.

en.L: A wound and dishonor he will find, \q and his reproach will not be wiped away.
en.B: Blows and disgrace will be his, \q and his shame will never be erased.
en.R: He will be beaten and shamed, \q and people will never forget what he did.

fr.L: Il trouvera coups et déshonneur, \q et son opprobre ne sera pas effacé.
fr.B: Il récoltera les coups et la honte, \q et son déshonneur ne s’effacera jamais.
fr.R: Il sera battu et couvert de honte, \q et les gens n’oublieront jamais ce qu’il a fait.

decisions.choice: a wound: blows, a beating
decisions.reason: The word (nega) is a blow or wound. The husband's revenge (verse 34) or public punishment may be in view.

source.text: כִּֽי־קִנְאָ֥ה חֲמַת־גָּ֑בֶר וְלֹֽא־יַ֝חְמ֗וֹל בְּי֣וֹם נָקָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For jealousy [is the] rage of a man, and he will not spare on [the] day of vengeance.

en.L: For jealousy [is the] fury of a man, \q and he will not spare on [the] day of vengeance.
en.B: For jealousy makes a husband furious, \q and when the day of revenge comes he will not hold back.
en.R: The woman's husband will be jealous and very angry. \q When he gets revenge, he will show no mercy.

fr.L: Car la jalousie [est] la fureur d’un homme, \q et il n’épargnera pas au jour de la vengeance.
fr.B: Car la jalousie rend un mari furieux, \q et le jour où il se vengera, il ne retiendra pas ses coups.
fr.R: Le mari de cette femme sera jaloux et très en colère. \q Quand il se vengera, il sera sans pitié.

decisions.choice: a man: the wronged husband
decisions.reason: The word (geber) means a man in his strength; here it is the husband of verse 29.

decisions.choice: a husband
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the man is, from verse 29.

source.text: לֹא־יִ֭שָּׂא פְּנֵ֣י כָל־כֹּ֑פֶר וְלֹֽא־יֹ֝אבֶ֗ה כִּ֣י תַרְבֶּה־שֹֽׁחַד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: He will not lift [the] face of any ransom, and he will not be willing though you multiply a bribe.

en.L: He will not regard any ransom, \q and he will not be willing, though you multiply [the] gift.
en.B: He will accept no payment to settle it, \q and no gift, however large, will satisfy him.
en.R: He will not take any money to forget it. \q No matter how much you offer him, he will not agree.

fr.L: Il n’aura égard à aucune rançon, \q et il ne consentira pas, même si tu multiplies le présent.
fr.B: Il n’acceptera aucun paiement pour régler l’affaire, \q et aucun cadeau, si grand soit-il, ne l’apaisera.
fr.R: Il ne prendra pas d’argent pour oublier. \q Peu importe ce que tu lui offriras, il refusera.

decisions.choice: lift the face of a ransom: accept a payment
decisions.reason: To "lift the face" is to show favor or accept (Genesis 32:20). A ransom (kopher) was a payment that settled a wrong (Exodus 21:30). Unlike the thief, the adulterer cannot buy his way out.

decisions.choice: be willing: the verb of 1:10
decisions.reason: The husband will not be willing (abah), as the son was not to be willing to go with sinners (1:10).
